0.0: I've sat in this desert for a long time, and no one else has talked to me except you... And no one has offered to help me as much as you...\r\n#L0# #b Have you seen a fox?
0.1: A fox? I've seen some rabbits and #o2100108#s, but not a single fox... Why do you need a fox? For you, I'll do anything to help. \r\n#L0# #b Nah, I don't need anything. Aren't you lonely out here by yourself?
0.2: I am lo-- actually, no, I am not. I'm not, since you're here with me. Maybe I arrived in this desert just to meet someone like you... I do feel like that sometimes. \r\n#L0# #bHave you ever thought of returning to where you came from?
0.3: I don't know... I do want to return home...but...that means I won't be able to see you anymore. The only reason this desert is even remotely seem beautiful to me is because you're here. \r\n#L0# #b Am I your friend?
0.4: Friend...? Is this what friendship is like...?

yes.0: Honestly, this is the first time I've ever made a true friend. A friend... I like...being friends with someone. I'm so happy. You ARE a friend.
yes.1: As a way to celebrate our friendship, I'll give you this book. I feel like you need it for some reason. Hopefully this will help.

no.0: A friend... Can a rose be a friend?

1.0: Wow, you got the storybook of #p2101006#! How is #p2101006#? Was he with a fox? What? He gave you the book after you told him you want to be his friend? Ah, so that's how the story found its equilibrium. I'm glad that happened.

yes.0: You acted as the fox to #p2101006#, so the story of #p2101006# has straightened its course. Thank you so much. This will also help put #m222020000# back on course.

npc.0: Someone out there needs this book. I can feel it. You should give the book to that person.

item.0: I don't think you've gotten the #bstorybook of #p2101006##k yet. Please observe #b#p2101006##k and discover what he's missing... If you can fill the void, he'll give you the storybook of #p2101006#.

lost.0: Oh... You lost the book... That's okay. I'll give you another one. We're friends, right?

QuestInfo.2: When you told #p2040052# you promised to be friends with #p2101006#, he let out a sigh of relief and thanked you for your efforts. Hopefully this straightened out the distorted part in the book #p2101006#. It feels weird being a part of a folk tale...
